Sunil vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41747) on 10 October,
2024

Bench: Rajendra Prakash Soni [2024:RJ-JD:41747]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 12496/2024 Sunil S/o Late Devilal, Aged About 21 Years, R/o Pipalipada Sarvan, Police Station Danpur, Dist. Banswara.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(At Present Lodged At Banswara Jail)
 ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through PP 2. Huki Charpota W/o Bahadur Charpota, R/o Khedapada,
 Tamtiya Ada, Sadar, Banswara.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajesh Kumar For Respondent(s) : Mr. Shrawan Singh, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJENDRA PRAKASH SONI Order 10/10/2024 1.
Petitioner is lugged and locked in F.I.R No.25/2024 of Police Station Sadar, District Banswara, for the offence under Section(s) 363, 366, 376(2)(N) of the I.P.C. and Section 5(th)/6 of POCSO Act.
He has filed this application for restoration of liberty under section 483 of BNSS (Section 439 of the old Code).
2. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record carefully.

3. Having given anxious consideration to the rival submissions and having examined the record, the argument raised by learned counsel for the petitioner is to the effect that victim was a consented party to the alleged offence.
He has invited attention of the court towards statement of victim recorded under Section 164 [2024:RJ-JD:41747] (2 of 2) [CRLMB-12496/2024] of Cr.P.C.

But,
under the POCSO Act consent of the victim has no legal value and cannot be a defence for the petitioner.

Sunil vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41747) on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37087612/
1 4.

In view of the enormous prima facie material placed on record in respect of the applicant, the allegations leveled against the petitioner, I am of the considered view that looking to the nature and gravity of the accusation in the instant case, the role attributed to the petitioner, the antecedents of the applicant and the case set up against petitioner in its entirety, the petitioner is not found entitled to be released on bail.

5. As a consequence of the above discussion, this Court is not inclined to extend indulgence of bail to the petitioners under Section 439 Cr.P.C. and hence, the instant Bail Application stands dismissed as being devoid of merit.
However, anything observed hereinabove shall not be treated as an expression of opinion on merits of the case and is meant for the purpose of deciding the present petition only.

Sunil vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41747) on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37087612/
2
